8 Official Government Portals Every Indian Business Owner Should Know

India runs eight main official business services online, from GST to State shop licences.

3 min read•

Last updated: 2 Oct 2026

S
Samjho Content Team
Finance and policy experts with 5+ years of experience helping Indians understand money, documents and government schemes.

Quick Summary

India runs eight main official business services online, from GST to State shop licences. Each one sits on a government-managed portal. This guide puts all eight in one place so you know exactly where to go, what each portal does and which level of government runs it.

What This Guide Covers

India runs eight main official business services online. Each one lives on a government portal. This guide lists all eight in one place, so you know exactly where to go.

Using the right portal matters. A registration done on a look-alike site is wasted effort. Many of these services are free on the official site.

The 8 Official Portals

1. GST Portal (gst.gov.in)

Cross the GST threshold and you must register here. The portal takes your registration application, monthly or quarterly returns, tax payments and refund claims. Small businesses can also check GST status and download certificates.

2. MCA21 (mca.gov.in)

Companies and LLPs are registered here. Annual filings, director changes and DIN updates also happen here. Starting a private limited company?

You use it for name approval, SPICe+ forms and compliance certificates.

3. Udyam Registration (udyamregistration.gov.in)

This is the free MSME registration. Aadhaar and PAN details are checked online. The certificate is permanent, so no renewal is needed.

Registered MSMEs can access scheme benefits and priority-sector lending.

4. MY MSME (my.msme.gov.in)

This Ministry of MSME portal carries schemes, notifications and grievance support. You can check scheme eligibility, download forms and follow Ministry announcements.

5. Startup India (startupindia.gov.in)

Apply here for DPIIT recognition if you run an eligible startup. The portal also explains tax benefits and funding schemes. The recognition certificate helps with government tenders and scheme applications.

6. Government e-Marketplace (gem.gov.in)

GeM is the government's own online marketplace. Sellers register, complete vendor assessment and brand registration, then list products and services. Ministries, departments and PSUs buy from here.

7. DGFT (dgft.gov.in)

This portal is for importers and exporters. You get your IEC (Importer Exporter Code) here. You also apply for licences, use e-scrips and read trade policy notices.

8. State and UT Services (india.gov.in/services/state)

State-level licences sit here, such as shop licences, labour registrations and trade permits. The page links you to your own State's portal. Check it first so you apply to the correct department.

Pick the Right Portal

  • Want GST registration? Go to the GST Portal.
  • Want to register a company or LLP? Go to MCA21.
  • Want MSME registration? Go to Udyam Registration.
  • Want DPIIT startup recognition? Go to Startup India.
  • Want to sell to government buyers? Go to GeM.
  • Want to import or export? Go to DGFT.
  • Want State shop or labour licences? Go to the National Portal State/UT Services page.

Key Points to Remember

  • GST registration, returns and payments happen only on gst.gov.in.
  • Company and LLP incorporation happens through MCA21 on mca.gov.in.
  • Udyam registration is free and permanent. Never pay an agent for it.
  • DPIIT recognition on Startup India opens up tax benefits and government tenders.
  • Sellers register on GeM to bid for government purchase orders.
  • Importers and exporters need an IEC code from DGFT before shipping goods.
  • State licences are found through the National Portal State/UT services page.
  • GST returns are due monthly or quarterly. Check the due-date calendar on the GST Portal.
  • MCA annual filings are due within 30 days of the AGM. Confirm this year's dates on mca.gov.in.
  • Startup India recognition is open all year. Scheme-specific windows are announced on the portal.

Eligibility

  • Businesses above the GST threshold must register on the GST Portal.
  • Companies and LLPs are registered through the MCA21 portal.
  • Micro, small and medium enterprises can register on Udyam.
  • DPIIT recognition on Startup India is open to eligible startups.
  • Sellers can register on GeM to bid for government purchase orders.
  • Importers and exporters need an IEC from DGFT before shipping goods.

Benefits

  • Registered MSMEs can access scheme benefits and priority-sector lending.
  • DPIIT recognition gives a certificate used for government tenders and scheme applications.
  • The Startup India portal also shares information on tax benefits and funding schemes.
  • Sellers on GeM can bid on government purchase orders.
  • Small businesses can check GST status and download certificates on the GST Portal.
  • MY MSME lets you check scheme eligibility and download official forms.

Required Documents

  • Keep PAN, Aadhaar and bank details ready before you start GST registration.
  • Udyam registration validates your Aadhaar and PAN details online.

How to Apply

  1. For GST, apply on gst.gov.in and then file monthly or quarterly returns there.
  2. For a company or LLP, use MCA21 for name approval, SPICe+ forms and compliance certificates.
  3. For MSME status, register free on udyamregistration.gov.in with Aadhaar and PAN.
  4. For MY MSME, visit the portal to check scheme eligibility and download forms.
  5. For startup recognition, apply on startupindia.gov.in with your incorporation details.
  6. For government selling, register on gem.gov.in, finish vendor assessment and brand registration, then list your products and services.
  7. For import or export, get your IEC on dgft.gov.in and use it for licence applications and e-scrips.
  8. For State licences, open india.gov.in/services/state, pick your State and apply on its official portal.

Important Dates

  1. GST returns are due monthly or quarterly. Check the due-date calendar on the GST Portal.
  2. MCA annual filings for companies are due within 30 days of the AGM. Confirm the current year dates on mca.gov.in.
  3. Startup India recognition is open year-round. Scheme-specific windows are announced on the portal.

Common Mistakes

  • Do not register on look-alike websites. Registrations done there are wasted effort.
  • Never pay an agent for Udyam registration. It is free and permanent on the official portal.
  • Find the correct State department before you apply for a shop, labour or trade licence.

FAQs

Which portal should I use for GST registration?
Use the GST Portal at gst.gov.in. Registration is free there, so avoid third-party sites that charge you. Keep PAN, Aadhaar and bank details ready before you start.
Is Udyam registration free?
Yes. Registration on udyamregistration.gov.in is free and stays valid forever. The Udyam certificate replaces the older Udyog Aadhaar and does not need renewal.
How do I get DPIIT startup recognition?
Apply on startupindia.gov.in with your incorporation details. Eligible startups get a recognition certificate. You can use it for tax benefits and government scheme applications.
Can small businesses bid on government tenders?
Yes. Register as a seller on gem.gov.in, complete vendor assessment and bid on live purchase orders. Many tenders keep relaxed eligibility rules for MSMEs and startups.
Where do I find my State's business licences?
Open the National Portal State/UT services page at india.gov.in/services/state and pick your State. It links you to the official State portals for shop licences, labour registrations and trade permits.
